title: Sardanapalus
summary: Sardanapalus is dated in Raleigh's chronological table (1617), column Assyria, by a yeere of the World. No tier 1–4 chronology dates this person.
description: Added from the Raleigh import (The History of the World, 1617). Raleigh is display-only. He gives a yeere of the World, not a BC year, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year. Raleigh is display-only and is not converted to BC.

death.date: The death of Sardanapalus happened A. M. 3257
death.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 171 (facsimile PDF p. 267)
death.note: The Assyrian king at the end of the empire in Shuckford’s title. Attached to the person Raleigh’s table already has, not to Cory’s sardanapallus. See open question K9.

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 788a
reign.note: Year cell "3868 3186 193". The third printed figure 193 is the column "Temple", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 20 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row. Column: Assyria.

reign.date: “altogether thirty in their generations to Sardanapalus”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 83; Ktesias, ap. Diodorus Siculus, book 2
reign.note: Thirty generations. Not a personal reign length.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 83; Ktesias, ap. Diodorus Siculus, book 2
reign.note: The empire remained with the Assyrians upwards of 1,360 years, until the time of Sardanapalus. Not his personal reign.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 190; Velleius Paterculus, Roman History, book 1, chapter 6
reign.note: The Asiatic empire. Not a personal reign of Ninus or of Sardanapalus.

reign.date: “the thirty-third in succession from Ninus and Semiramis”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 190; Velleius Paterculus, Roman History, book 1, chapter 6
reign.note: Sardanapalus. semiramis-i was not used. The fragment does not say Semiramis I.
